title: What does the XRPL DefaultRipple account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DefaultRipple and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DefaultRipple enables rippling by default on an account's trust lines. [1]

Issuers generally need rippling so holders can transfer their issued tokens, while ordinary holders have different risk considerations. The setting affects defaults; existing line-specific NoRipple state still deserves inspection. Rippling concerns how balances flow through connected trust lines, not permission for any agent to spend the holder's wallet or a promise that all paths have liquidity. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DefaultRipple and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DefaultRipple is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
